metadata.mirror:about: MASTER-OUTWARD.svg — the MIRROR chain of the project. All exports / served surfaces / downstream effects / what we publish to the world. Every node has a forward counterpart in MASTER-INWARD.svg via the matching mirror:id attribute. Updates on one side propagate to the other via the gently-mirror-pair contract. See: /data/Projects/MySpace++/REFLECTION.md
metadata.mirror:crystal-method: sha256(forward_bytes XOR mirror_bytes), zero-pad shorter to longer; v1 method. Daemon will switch to blake3-FNV-interleave once shipped.
metadata.mirror:updated-by: gently (main) — SYNC-7 practice update; bumped index-published node to reflect 208,550 Kimi entries (was implicit ~38k); pair crystal verified manually via python xor+sha256.

g.text: ⟲ MASTER-OUTWARD.svg — the MIRROR chain · all egress · effects on consumers
paired with MASTER-INWARD.svg via mirror:id · updates one side reflect to the other · crystal = XOR of both chains
Layer 0 — downstream consumers (what eats our bytes)
other projects can mirror our index
we are HF's lazy mirror, NOT its host
no SPA · no ads · no logins
no two sessions step on each other
audit trail = which agent_uuid did this
READ keys see read surfaces only
no login wall, no consent dialog
cannot be displaced by compute alone
Layer 1 — agentic egress flows (how chain ops become served surfaces)
Layer 2 — served artifacts (what consumers see as the rendered system)
consumer can replay with same seed
routes to one of ~22 frontier models
we choose best model for the task
Layer 3 — read endpoints (what consumers query for state)
consumer: user sees state in 5-10 terms
no two sessions step on each other
friends with READ key see their proj
HTTP Range to actual HF on demand
future Claude session loads MEMORY.md index
no other agents read this dir
via: auto-memory Read on session start
Layer 4 — 6 constitutional principles (what consumers can verify offline)
consumer verifies bb hash → matches release
if mismatch: refuse to trust crystal
consumer matches against published binary hash
re-run defense: stamp differs across versions
sessions publish as ONE chain extension
consumer sees committed deltas, not active stream
consumer verifies block existed at that time
runtime never blocks on BTC RPC
Layer 5 — mirror bridge to MASTER-INWARD.svg (every node above has a forward counterpart)
how the reflection works (this side = mirror chain; sister SVG = forward chain)
1. every node here declares mirror:id matching exactly one mspc:src-id / flow-id / construct-id / store-id / principle-id in MASTER-INWARD.svg
2. when the forward side updates (a new flow lands, a new file is ingested, a new principle change), the daemon
propagates the change to the matching node here by mutating data-* attrs + the metadata crystal hash
3. the daemon NEVER reshapes the layout — only the bound data fields change
4. both SVGs share a single chain-of-truth: SealedChain { forward = INWARD, mirror = OUTWARD, crystal = XOR(fwd, mir) }
5. updating either side without the other breaks the crystal — the gently-mirror-pair daemon refuses to extend until repaired
6. consumer-facing surfaces here (Layer 0-3) are LIVE — what visitors / friends / agents actually see and query
7. provenance proofs here (Layer 4) let consumers VERIFY the chain offline against the published constitutional invariants
8. effects this side carries (downstream consumers) are first-class: every surface declares both consumer and source
MASTER-OUTWARD.svg v1.0.0 · the mirror chain · paired with MASTER-INWARD.svg · crystal axiom: INWARD ⊕ OUTWARD = SealedChain.crystal
